Formula SAE / Mk.7 / seat design & fabrication

Designed and fabricated the 5052-H32 aluminum driver seat for the Mk.7 Formula SAE car. The project connects a perforated pan, back, and folded sides to their cockpit context; the supporting analysis image is retained without a numerical result.
Designed and fabricated the Mk.7 driver seat.
The Mk.7 seat geometry uses perforated panels and folded sides.
I designed and made the Mk.7 driver seat.
The work presented here covers the seat’s design and its fabrication for the Mk.7 car.
LiDAR scanner
LiDAR scanner

Built an eversion platform for three soft-vine body geometries and frequent specimen changes. Initial testing reached 1.2 psi with deformation and connection failures, prompting aluminum and steel reinforcement. The reinforced vessel is designed for 34 kPa (5 psi), backed by FEA rather than a 5 psi pressure test: about 3.3× the 1.5 psi maximum working pressure. The platform supported a 45-run experiment with directly measured contact force.

Targets: a 34 kPa (5 psi) design pressure, a 3.33 factor of safety over the 10.3 kPa (1.5 psi) maximum working pressure; accept up to 571 mm (22.5 in) body circumference; swap bodies for more than 15 daily trials.

Reinforcement FEA at 500 lbf per face (5.8 psi): 6.524 mm maximum deformation and 0.2339 GPa maximum stress versus A36 steel's 0.25 GPa yield. The vine outlet remains weakest. This FEA backs the 5 psi design pressure; the reinforced vessel has not been pressure-tested at 5 psi.
AURA swerve drive
Mechanical Engineer

Built and iterated a two-week line-following robot around an Arduino Mega and 14 reflectance channels. Switched from 4 mm to 8 mm sensor pitch, revised feedback control, and reduced mass from 428 g to 284 g. The best recorded lap was 18 s on the course, short of the under-15-second target.
18 s on the Spa-Francorchamps-inspired track; the original under-15-second target was not reached.
4 mm sensor spacing was tested first; 8 mm spacing was then selected to increase the usable line-detection range in sharp turns.
3.4, 6.9 and 10.3 kPa (0.5, 1.0 and 1.5 psi) define the three experimental pressure settings; 1.5 psi is the maximum working pressure.
